source.title: Advisory on Kleptocracy and Foreign Public Corruption (FIN-2022-A001)

summary: FinCEN advisory urging financial institutions to detect proceeds of foreign public corruption and kleptocracy, with particular focus on Russia given the nexus of corruption, sanctions evasion and the invasion of Ukraine. It describes bribery/extortion of foreign officials, misappropriation/embezzlement of public assets, and laundering of illicit proceeds through shell companies, offshore accounts, and purchases of U.S. real estate, luxury goods and other high-value assets. It gives case examples (TENEX/TLI, Odebrecht/Braskem, Belarus, El Salvador, Peskov family) and lists financial red flag indicators, plus SAR/BSA filing guidance including the key term 'CORRUPTION FIN-2022-A001'.

citations.quote: Bribery schemes often involve payments to foreign government officials by persons and entities to obtain or retain business, or for other benefits.
the defendant, Mark Lambert, participated in a scheme to bribe Vadim Mikerin, a Russian official at JSC Techsnabexport (TENEX), a subsidiary of Russia’s State Atomic Energy Corporation

typologies.label: Misappropriation or Embezzlement of Public Assets

citations.quote: Misappropriation or embezzlement of public assets broadly encompass the theft, diversion, or misuse of public funds or resources for personal benefit or enrichment.
Lukashenka, who was originally sanctioned in 2006, has rewarded businessmen close to him with benefits and privileges in exchange for kickbacks to himself and his regime.
Corrupt actors often use shell companies to obscure the ownership and origin of illicit funds.

these shell companies and offshore accounts are frequently established in foreign jurisdictions whose corporate formation regimes and financial sector offer limited transparency to law enforcement, regulators, or financial institutions.

typologies.label: Purchase of Real Estate, Luxury Goods and High-Value Assets to Launder Corruption Proceeds

citations.quote: Corrupt officials and others involved in bribery and other forms of corruption often purchase various U.S. assets, such as luxury real estate and hotels, private jets, artwork, and motion picture companies, to launder the proceeds of their corruption.
Peskov’s family is reported to own real estate in Russia and elsewhere valued at more than $10 million, and to have access to a number of luxury vehicles, including private aircrafts and yachts

typologies.label: Shared Beneficial Owner

citations.quote: Transactions involving long-term government contracts consistently awarded, through an opaque selection process, to the same legal entity or entities that share similar beneficial ownership structures.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Financial red flag indicators, page 8 (first bullet). PAT002 doctrine: 'identifies entities connected through a common beneficial owner, ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), controlling shareholder or ultimate controller,' with intelligence question 'Do two or more entities share the same beneficial owner?' The advisory's red flag describes exactly this mechanism applied to public procurement: nominally distinct bidders that in fact 'share similar beneficial ownership structures' repeatedly win the same government contracts through an opaque process -- a common hidden UBO/controller sitting behind multiple counterparties to capture state contracts, not merely a generic corruption reference.

typologies.label: Hidden Controller

citations.quote: Corrupt actors may also leverage their family members and close associates to create shell companies and open business or personal accounts on their behalf while retaining control of the accounts.
Assets held in the name of intermediate legal entities whose beneficial owner or owners are tied to a kleptocrat or his or her family member.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Shell Companies and Offshore Financial Accounts narrative, page 6; financial red flag indicators, page 9. PAT010 doctrine: identifies 'individuals or entities exercising effective control over an organisation despite not appearing as the declared owner, director or controller,' asking 'Who is actually controlling the entity or network?' The advisory describes precisely this split between nominal and true control: the kleptocrat places title with family members/associates or intermediate legal entities while 'retaining control of the accounts,' and the red flag explicitly instructs institutions to look past the declared beneficial owner to the kleptocrat actually directing the asset -- the concealed-control pattern PAT010 is built to surface, distinct from the shell-company-characteristics focus of the already-claimed PAT007.

extraction_notes: The Knowledge Centre library has no 'corruption' family typologies at all (list_typologies(family='corruption') returns empty, and searches for 'bribery', 'corruption', 'embezzlement', 'kleptocracy', 'misappropriation of public funds', and 'PEP'-related phrases all returned no match above the 0.25 floor). Three of the four typologies here are therefore emergent by necessity, not by weak evidence -- the document's own case support for them is strong. Only the shell-company/offshore-account laundering method matched an existing typology (PAT007 Shell Company Network, network family), and that match is a partial fit: PAT007's doctrine is about detecting shell-company network structural signatures, whereas the advisory's framing is corruption-proceeds laundering via such structures -- confidence set to medium for that link. Jurisdictions list includes all countries named as bribe destinations/shell-company domiciles in the Odebrecht (p.5) and TLI/TENEX (p.5) case studies even though the advisory's main narrative focus is Russia, Belarus and El Salvador; a reviewer may want to split 'named case jurisdictions' from 'primary threat jurisdictions' in a future schema revision. Indicator detectable_in_transaction_data judgments assume a monitoring stack without beneficial-ownership or document-image enrichment; systems with UBO/OCR enrichment could detect more of the documentary/network indicators than marked here.
